Cut off values for pruning the context tree of a VLMC with covariates

Source: R/covlmc.R
cutoff.covlmc.Rd

This function returns all the cut off values that should induce a pruning of the context tree of a VLMC with covariates.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'covlmc'
cutoff(model, raw = FALSE, tolerance = .Machine$double.eps^0.5, ...)

Arguments

model

a fitted COVLMC model.

raw

specifies whether the returned values should be limit values computed in the model or modified values that guarantee pruning (defaults to FALSE, see details).

tolerance

specifies the minimum separation between two consecutive values of the cut off in quantile scale (before any transformation). See details.

...

additional arguments for the cutoff function.

Value

a vector of cut off values in quantile scale (in decreasing order), NULL if none can be computed

Details

Notice that the list of cut off values returned by the function is not as complete as the one computed for a VLMC without covariates. Indeed, pruning the COVLMC tree creates new pruning opportunities that are not evaluated during the construction of the initial model, while all pruning opportunities are computed during the construction of a VLMC context tree. Nevertheless, the largest value returned by the function is guaranteed to produce the least pruned tree consistent with the reference one.

For large COVLMC, some cut off values can be almost identical, with a difference of the order of the machine epsilon value. The tolerance parameter is used to keep only values that are different enough. This is done in the quantile scale, before transformations implemented when raw is FALSE.

Notice that the native scale (log-likelihood ratio) is not directly useful in COVLMC as the differences in model sizes are not constant through the pruning process. As a consequence, unlike cutoff.vlmc(), this function does not provide a scale parameter: values are always given in quantile scale (i.e. as p-values of the likelihood ratio tests).

By default (raw = FALSE), the values are slightly smaller than the p-values of the likelihood ratio tests computed from the COVLMC (in quantile scale): they are reduced by a relative margin of tolerance / 2 (and by at least the smallest representable amount). prune.covlmc() estimates new logistic models and recomputes the likelihood ratio tests, whose p-values can differ in the last digits from the ones stored in the model, depending on the linear algebra library used by R. The margin ensures that pruning with a cut off value does have an effect on the model. As consecutive values differ by at least tolerance, the margin keeps each value larger than the next one. Setting raw to TRUE returns the p-values themselves.

As automated model selection is provided by tune_covlmc(), the direct use of cutoff should be reserved to advanced exploration of the set of trees that can be obtained from a complex one, e.g. to implement model selection techniques that are not provided by tune_covlmc().

See also

prune.covlmc() and tune_covlmc()

Examples

pc <- powerconsumption[powerconsumption$week == 5, ]
rdts <- cut(pc$active_power, breaks = c(0, quantile(pc$active_power, probs = c(0.5, 1))))
rdts_cov <- data.frame(day_night = (pc$hour >= 7 & pc$hour <= 17))
m_cov <- covlmc(rdts, rdts_cov, min_size = 5)
draw(m_cov)
#> ▪
#> ├─ (0,1.34]
#> │  ├─ (0,1.34]
#> │  │  ├─ (0,1.34] ([ -2.813 • 2.178 ⁞ -4.449 ⁞ 2.418 ])
#> │  │  └─ (1.34,7.54] ([ -19.57 • 18.39 ])
#> │  └─ (1.34,7.54] (0.8649, 0.1351)
#> └─ (1.34,7.54] (0.07341, 0.9266)
cutoff(m_cov)
#> [1] 0.02328831 0.01834317
## raw values are slightly larger than the default ones
cutoff(m_cov, raw = TRUE) - cutoff(m_cov)
#> [1] 1.735114e-10 1.366673e-10
## pruning with the largest cut off value
draw(prune(m_cov, alpha = cutoff(m_cov)[1]))
#> ▪
#> ├─ (0,1.34]
#> │  ├─ (0,1.34] ([ -2.759 • 2.785 ⁞ -2.525 ])
#> │  └─ (1.34,7.54] (0.8649, 0.1351)
#> └─ (1.34,7.54] (0.07341, 0.9266)
